title: Age to start trombone; slide trumpet
summary: Starting at eight, positions, and sliding trumpets tried by Oliver and others.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Before I forget, I want to ask about, in learning trombone, how young can you start?

A real little kid can teach it, could he? Yeah, you can start a little kid. You can start, well, about, say about eight years old. You can start a kid eight years old. And he'll make it. Like the violin.
I started, I played violin myself. I started on three-quarter sizes. Yeah, three-quarters, a little bit.
I got about twelve, I got a bigger one.
Uh-huh. But trombone is only the one size, isn't it?
Unless he got him one of them sliding corners. Yeah. Louis had one of those on the boat, I got a picture. Baby Dodds and Louis.

Joe Oliver tried to play one too, yeah. He had one. They didn't do no good though. I don't know why, but they couldn't make good on the sliding trumpet. There was one fellow, there was that guy, and he was a white fellow. He was playing the sliding trumpet, and he come through here with his shoulder. That guy could fool that thing. But I guess he must have been the trombone, ex-trombone player. Maybe. Yeah, he must have been. Yeah, he was really good. So the kid could start then at eight years old.
Oh yeah, he would start a kid at eight years old. He couldn't reach down to sixth and seventh position.

No, but as he'd go along, you see, you've got to give him anyhow about a year to get him straightened and teach him that position where that little toe is at and all like that. That's like a little girl playing piano. You can play that piano all over there, and if there's a key out, that girl play that piano and don't, she don't think about that key and play the whole piece. See, that key, you know, if it's out, dead key, you know, she'll play over that dead key. Now I couldn't go there and play it over somebody that plays piano. Couldn't hardly go, because the first thing they'd say, this piano's bad, it's missing keys. I can't play it, see? I can't go there, just go on and play it. Yeah.
